summary: 评论者肯定霍利斯的城市见闻，却质疑他过于乐观的结论。技术创新和城市活力的故事，难以回答贫富差距、建筑环境和治理的问题。
logic: 书评人介绍城市写作热潮与书中案例
为什么怀疑“城市有益”的乐观判断
用暴乱、不平等与街道空间检验论点
回到伦敦的地产投资与治理

paragraphs.brief: 一本厚重城市书面向谁
sentences: Don’t let that seductive 99p deceive you – with Leo Hollis’s Cities Are Good for You you’re definitely getting seventeen pounds’ worth of book; £17, and possibly somewhere approaching 17lbs as well, because this is a hefty tome, not quite lavishly tooled enough for the coffee table, but nor entirely a comfortable proposition when lying abed.
别被价格尾数那诱人的九十九便士骗了：利奥·霍利斯的《城市对你有好处》绝对值足十七英镑，没准也快有十七磅重，既不够精美到能当茶几书摆设，躺在床上读又嫌沉。
Which rather raises the question, who exactly is it aimed at?
这不免让人想问，这本书究竟写给谁看？
People who see the city as a backdrop of fashion plates against which they can strike physical and intellectual attitudes, or those for whom urbanism is just another wanky trend?
是写给那些把城市当作时尚背景、借以摆姿态或卖弄见识的人，还是写给那些只把城市主义当作又一股矫饰风潮的人？

Two years ago the world reached a tipping point, with more urban than rural inhabitants, and this is being reflected in the cultural superstructure: there are increasing numbers of books, films and TV and radio programmes about the city.
两年前，世界达到了一个临界点，城市居民多于农村居民，文化上层结构反映了这一点：关于城市的书籍、电影、电视和广播节目越来越多。
paragraphs.gist: 书评人从这本城市著作的价钱、重量及目标读者说起，把它放在全球城市人口超越农村人口后城市题材大增的背景中。

sentences: Hollis’s is a reasonably efficient addition to the genre – a comprehensive overview of the state of the city and contemporary thinking in urbanism.
作为一部全面梳理城市现状和当代城市思想的作品，霍利斯的书算是为这一体裁添了一本称职之作。

He begins and ends his tale – which takes the form of an extended multi-city-break – with musings occasioned by Manhattan’s High Line park, the curiously liminal green space established on the derelict elevated railway line that runs down the Lower West Side.
全书像一趟漫长的跨城旅行；开篇与结尾都是关于曼哈顿高线公园的随想，这片奇特的过渡绿地建在下西区一条废弃的高架铁路上。

In between, Hollis travels through time, giving a highly partisan and select history of urban theory and town planning; and through space, hopping from the US to Bangalore and Mumbai, to Shanghai, to Songdo in South Korea, Santiago in Chile and Bogotá in Colombia, then back home to his own Metroland on the outskirts of London for a little rest and reflection.
期间，他穿越时间，以鲜明立场选择性讲述城市理论和规划史，又穿越空间，从美国到班加罗尔、孟买、上海、韩国松岛、圣地亚哥及波哥大，最后回到伦敦郊外的家中休整反思。
paragraphs.gist: 霍利斯以曼哈顿高线公园首尾照应，穿梭各国城市和规划史，而书评人认为这是一次覆盖面广却颇有取舍的城市理论巡览。

paragraphs.brief: 新兴城市案例的报道价值
sentences: At its best Cities Are Good for You resembles a collection of readable feature articles on contemporary cities.
《城市对你有好处》最精彩的部分，读起来像一组描写当代城市的生动特写。

Hollis is informative about public transport in South America and the economics of Mumbai’s infamous Dharavi – a slum that, once penetrated, is exposed as not just a colourful backdrop for fictional slumdog millionaires, but a complex and curiously efficient human anthill.
霍利斯介绍了南美的公共交通和孟买达拉维贫民区的经济；深入其中才会发现，这里除了是电影故事的鲜活背景，还是一个繁复却出奇高效的人类聚居地。

He also covers Chinese urbanisation well, carefully describing the punitive Hukou system of residential registration that allows for the ever-accelerating migration from rural areas, while simultaneously ensuring that these former peasants can be maintained in a state of perpetual peonage.
他也细致描述了中国城市化和严苛的户籍制度，指出农村人口进城的速度可以不断加快，这些昔日的农民却仍可能长期处于从属地位。
Hollis is at pains to retain a global perspective, writing more about the cities of the emergent BRICK economies than he does about the boring old bricks-and-mortar town I live in.
为保持全球视野，他写新兴经济体城市的篇幅，超过了描写书评人所住老城市的篇幅。

He rightly sees the future of the city as being shaped by developments to the east and the south, where the megalopolises of the 21st century will – or so late capitalism’s flag-wavers believe – arise, replete with gleaming towers worthy of Oz.
他正确地看到，东方和南方的发展正在塑造城市的未来；至少在晚期资本主义的拥护者看来，二十一世纪的超级城市将在那里崛起，摩天塔楼如奥兹国般闪耀。
paragraphs.gist: 书中写南美交通、孟买贫民区经济和中国户籍制度的部分尤其精彩，展现新兴经济体的城市如何塑造全球都市的未来。

paragraphs.brief: 空泛乐观与语言陈词滥调
sentences: But at its worst Cities Are Good for You is a pretty vulgar garment; an appliqué of Panglossian optimism and theoretical banality stitched together by stylistic cliché.
但在最差处，这本书像件俗丽的拼贴衣裳：盲目的乐观、平庸的理论，靠陈词滥调缝在一起。
Does it matter that in a book about cities the author uses such expressions – quite without irony – as “vibrant art scene”?
在一本关于城市的书中，作者使用这种表达方式作为“充满活力的艺术场景”是否重要？

Well, yes, I think it does, just as writing the sentence: “For centuries the city has been the perfect place to develop the killer app” should’ve at least given Hollis’s editor cause for thoughts of the form: what was I put on earth for, if not to excise anachronistic drivel like this?
书评人觉得当然要紧：把“几百年来城市都是开发杀手级应用的理想场所”写进书里，编辑难道不该问自己，删掉这种时代错置的胡话不正是本职吗？
But then this is a writer who will never use the expression “low tax” when he can reach for that providential euphemism “light touch fiscal policy”.
不过，只要能用上“温和干预的财政政策”这个恰到好处的委婉说法，这位作者就绝不会直说“低税”。
To seriously tackle his infelicities and solecisms would’ve placed someone in the unenviable position of a barber shaving a dog: where do you stop?
真要一处处改正他那些用词失当的地方，就像理发师给狗剃毛，让人不知该在哪里收手。
paragraphs.gist: 书评人批评霍利斯用俗套、时代错置的表达和华丽委婉语包装乐观判断，甚至令编辑难知从何删改。

paragraphs.brief: 城市有益的断言忽视谁
sentences: I think the problem with Cities Are Good for You derives from its title.
我认为，《城市对你有好处》的问题从书名就开始了。
It doesn’t matter whether the emphasis is placed on “are” or not, the end result is that I – or indeed you – feel hectored.
无论重音是否落在“有”字上，读者最后都难免觉得被人训了一通。

Try telling the single mother with children who has just had to leave London because of the new benefit cap that cities are good for her; or why not convey the advantages of a vibrant art scene to the urbanites who live in the shanty towns of Lagos and Johannesburg, or the slums of Jakarta and Dhaka?
不妨去对因为福利上限而刚被迫带孩子离开伦敦的单亲母亲说“城市对你有好处”，或者去向拉各斯、约翰内斯堡、雅加达和达卡贫民区的居民解释“蓬勃的艺术生活”对他们有什么好处。

Even at the level of what objectively are high-class problems, there are still those of us who experience on a daily basis profound alienation from the city – from its moiling crowds and roiling psychic miasmas, from its chilly depersonalisation and its fervid marketisation – an alienation that we yet feel perversely ambivalent about, loving and hating it as we love the cities that produce such powerful feelings.
即便在条件较好的人当中，也有人每天都因拥挤的人群、压迫感、冷漠疏离和狂热的市场化而深感异化，对能激起如此强烈感情的城市，反倒既爱又恨。
paragraphs.gist: “城市有益于你”的断语让书评人感到被说教，因为高房租、贫民窟和城市疏离感会令许多居民既依恋城市又深受其苦。

paragraphs.brief: 书名束缚了对城市的判断
sentences: For clap-happy Hollis there can be no such ambivalence, nor are there any ambiguities.
一味为城市叫好的霍利斯容不下这种矛盾心情，也不承认其中有多少暧昧之处。

He may begin his excursus with a view of the city as an organic phenomenon, perhaps one not best understood by rationalist thought, but by concepts derived from the sociobiology of EO Wilson et al, yet his daft title pulls him back time and again to a simplistic meliorism of the form: cities are good for you – and you had better work really hard to ensure that they are (and by extension to validate the title of my book).
他起初或许把城市当作有机现象，尝试借威尔逊等人的社会生物学概念来理解它；可那个武断的书名总把他拉回简单的进步信念：城市对你有好处，而你最好努力让事实果真如此，好替书名作证。
paragraphs.gist: 霍利斯虽把城市描述成复杂有机体，却受书名立场所限，屡屡回到“只要努力城市就会对人有益”的简单结论。

paragraphs.brief: 承认难题却缺少有力对策
sentences: It’s not that Hollis doesn’t acknowledge the downside of cities – he includes a section on the 2011 London riots, and is not unsympathetic to the malcontents.
霍利斯也承认城市的阴暗面；他专门写了2011年伦敦骚乱，对心怀不满的人并非毫无同情。
Nor does he ignore the implications of the Gini coefficient, which indicates that widening inequality may be an ineluctable aspect of larger and larger conurbations.
他也注意到基尼系数所提示的问题：都市圈规模越大，不平等加剧就越可能是难以避免的现象。

Yet behind all this apparent balance lies a curious kind of neoliberal civic virtuousness – Hollis says that for the city to remain good for us it must address three primary problems: sustainability, trust and inequality.
然而，在所有这些明显的平衡背后，有一种奇怪的新自由主义公民道德 — — Hollis说，为了让城市对我们保持良好，它必须解决三个主要问题：可持续性、信任和不平等。

He acknowledges that the balm for the festering urban sores so painfully anatomised by Mike Davis in his Planet of Slums cannot be found in the market, and yet what he offers is no real alternative, but rather a hotchpotch of bike-hire schemes and superannuated hippies growing tomatoes on Brooklyn rooftops.
他承认市场治不好迈克·戴维斯在《贫民窟的星球》中剖析的城市顽疾，却也没有给出真正的替代方案，只有自行车租赁计划和布鲁克林屋顶上种番茄的老嬉皮士之类零散的例子。
In part this has to be attributable to his Manichean and partial view of urbanism and urban development.
这部分源于他对城市主义和城市发展的看法片面，习惯于把人物简单分成好与坏两类。
For Hollis the mantra is: Jane Jacobs and “soft modernist” Patrick Geddes good; Le Corbusier and Robert Moses (who are seen crudely as counterparts) bad, bad, bad!
对Hollis来说，咒语是：简·雅各布和“软现代主义者”帕特里克·盖德斯好；勒·科布西耶和罗伯特·摩西(被粗鲁地视为对手)坏、坏、坏和坏!
paragraphs.gist: 霍利斯承认骚乱和不平等，也提出可持续性、信任与公平等难题，但书评人认为零散的社区项目和对规划者非善即恶的评判不足以回应它们。

paragraphs.brief: 规划者功过须放回时代
sentences: It’s true enough that the legacy of the pioneering urban activist and theorist Jacobs is due for a re-evaluation.
先驱性的城市活动家、理论家简·雅各布斯留下的遗产，确实值得重新评价。
Her key work The Life and Death of Great American Cities eloquently makes the case for communitarianism trumping dirigisme long before “stakeholder” was a twinkle in Tony Blair’s eye.
早在“利益相关者”成为托尼·布莱尔的时髦用语之前，她的代表作《美国大城市的死与生》就已雄辩说明，社区自发的力量胜过自上而下的管制。

Jacobs viewed the “eyes on the street”, and the sidewalk “ballet” of her Greenwich Village neighbourhood as key to an understanding of how cities can happily and safely function, and she took up the cudgels against the New York city planner Robert Moses, who was intent on driving an expressway through this happily cosmopolitan district.
雅各布斯从格林威治村的“街道眼”和人行道上的“芭蕾”看到了城市安全、和谐运行的关键；她因此挺身反对纽约规划者罗伯特·摩西修建高速路贯穿这个多元社区的计划。

But to condemn Moses out of hand as a proponent of autogeddon is facile in the extreme, as is Hollis’s determination to demonise Le Corbusier as a modernist Moloch intent on feeding the children of the proletariat into high-rise sarcophaguses.
但把摩西一概斥为汽车城市灾难的推手，或把勒·柯布西耶妖魔化成要将劳工子女塞进高层“石棺”的现代主义怪物，都太过简单。

Ultimately, all these people were seeking solutions to particular problems at given stages of cities’ development – Moses zoned for parks and public housing because these were what New Yorkers needed; initially he was a hero of the people.
这些人其实都在寻找解决各自时代城市问题的办法：摩西规划公园与公屋是因为纽约人当时需要它们，他起初是民众心中的英雄。

As for Le Corbusier, by his works shall you know him, and frankly I’d rather read a single paragraph of his pellucid and revolutionary prose than a whole chapter of Hollis’s bumf, no matter how packed the latter is with useful information.
至于勒·柯布西耶，不妨从作品认识他；书评人宁愿读他一段清晰而富改革精神的文字，也不愿读霍利斯一整章空话，即使其中塞满有用信息。
paragraphs.gist: 雅各布斯维护街道生活固有价值，但书评人认为摩西和勒·柯布西耶也在回应特定时代的住房或规划需求，不宜一概丑化。

paragraphs.brief: 建筑材质与身体感受被忽略
sentences: Then there’s the built environment; for someone prepared to spend 400 pages telling us how great cities are, Hollis seems remarkably untouched by the aesthetics of buildings.
然后是建筑环境；对于一个准备花费400页来告诉我们城市有多伟大的人来说，Hollis似乎完全没有受到建筑美学的影响。

Say what you will about Le Corbusier, he did know how to design a beautiful building; and modernism was a genuine response to the technological zeitgeist, and often an attempt to remake the city as a haptic phenomenon.
不管怎么看勒·柯布西耶，他的确懂得设计漂亮的建筑；现代主义回应了当时的技术精神，也常试图让人从触觉重新体验城市。
(Think of the wood grain impressed into the brutalist concrete beams of the Hayward Gallery.)
想想海沃德美术馆那些粗野主义混凝土梁上压印的木纹就知道了。

I tend to think of cities first and foremost in this sensual way, and to register my response to them by my transit of the urban scape; whereas for Hollis the flaneur is, presumably, a rather recondite – if not irrelevant – figure, although he professes to be a great urban walker himself.
我总先从这种感官体验来理解城市，在穿行街景时体会自己的反应；霍利斯虽自称喜欢在城里步行，却似乎认为“城市漫游者”这个形象晦涩，甚至无关紧要。
paragraphs.gist: 书评人喜欢步行时亲身感受城市的材质和建筑美感，却认为霍利斯虽自称热爱步行，对这些触觉与视觉细节着墨太少。

paragraphs.brief: 对社交科技的热捧遭讽刺
sentences: In place of this shifting, evanescent and endlessly creative perspective of the city, we are offered a lot of wittering about Twitter.
读者没能看到这样流动、瞬息变化而富有创造力的城市视角，倒是听到了不少关于推特的絮叨。

During Hollis’s extended paean to the delights of Call-me-Dave’s “silicon roundabout” in London’s hipper-than-thou Shoreditch, I kept being reminded of that YouTube sensation “The Dickhead Song”, which mercilessly satirises the “creatives” of east London, and in particular of its rousing chorus: “I love my life as a dickhead / All my friends are dickheads too …” Because all sorts of dickheads meet with Hollis’s approval – including the mayor of London – while he’s never happier than when extolling the virtues of the latest killer app.
霍利斯长篇赞美伦敦肖尔迪奇的“硅岛”，让我想起网上那首嘲弄东伦敦“创意人士”的歌；他几乎谁都叫好，包括伦敦市长，而赞颂最新的热门应用更让他乐此不疲。
paragraphs.gist: 霍利斯热捧推特、科技创意区和新应用的语调令书评人想起讽刺东伦敦创意圈的歌曲，觉得这些内容取代了更鲜活的城市体验。

paragraphs.brief: 地方财权与城市包容性受损
sentences: In truth, the real killer app in the city where Hollis and I are both domiciled is the light fiscal touch – insignificant local tax-raising powers – and the sham it makes of a true local democracy.
其实，在我和霍利斯同住的伦敦，真正起决定作用的是所谓“轻触式”财政政策：地方政府几乎没有征税权，真正的地方民主因而成了空谈。

It’s a killer app that’s murdered the municipal socialism that once made London a livable city for people of all classes, and has left the way open for the city to increasingly resemble Mayor Bloomberg’s zero-tolerance-for-the-poor Manhattan.
这种政策扼杀了曾让各个阶层都能在伦敦生活的市政社会主义，也让伦敦越来越像彭博任内几乎容不下穷人的曼哈顿。
I don’t imagine these developments – taking place in cities all over Britain – will be good for you, no matter the gloss this handsomely produced book puts on them.
我不认为这些发展 — — 发生在英国各地的城市 — — 会对你有好处，无论这本英俊的书给人留下什么光彩。
paragraphs.gist: 最后，书评人以伦敦地方征税权薄弱和城市贫困者的处境为例，认为漂亮的书页掩盖不了当地民主与包容性正在受损。
